text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
- According to a survey by public television's OBOP polling agency, 90 percent of Poles favour their country's entry into NATO and 88 percent into the European Union.

- Polish insurance companies will be able to invest abroad. Yesterday a government legislative committee decided insurers will be allowed to invest up to five percent of their funds in certain countries.

- The opposition Solidarity Election Action (AWS) and the co-ruling Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) are tied for first place, with 26 percent support, in a pre-election poll by Pracownia Badan Spolecznych organisation. The Peasant party (PSL) got 15 percent, and the opposition Union for Freedom (UW) and Movement for the Reconstruction of Poland (ROP) 10 percent.

- The Senate National Economy Committee proposed more than a dozen amendments to the 1997 budget bill which would increase budget revenues by about 60 million zlotys and spending by 90 million. The Senate will vote today on the changes.

- The results of Poland's iron and steel industry last year were much worse than in 1995. In 1996 gross profits of mills totalled 33.5 million zlotys compared with 740.7 million in 1995 and net profits were 21.5 million after 339.9 million in 1995.
- According to glass maker Krosno SA's management, this year the firm's sales will total 213 million zlotys, an 18.5 percent increase over 1996. Net profit will be unchanged at 10.05 million zlotys.

- At a general meeting on March 10, the management of the Bank Rozwoju Cukrownictwa sugar development bank will seek approval for an issue of new shares totalling 15.2 million zlotys. The issue could bring a doubling of the bank's share capital.

- Traders, business circles and analysts praised the government decision to free fuel prices, but they fear a rise in inflation. According to Miroslaw Gronicki from the Market Economy Research Institute the decision will increase inflation which will this year certainly exceed the 13 percent target.
- Rolimpex is seeking to purchase a package of shares in the Ropczyce sugar mill. Rolimpex wants to remain the largest firm in this market sector, its deputy president Andrzej Budzinski said.

- Nine companies, most of which are foreign, have expressed interest in cooperation with boiler maker Rafako SA. In early January the firm's management said the company wants a strategic partnership with a leading electromechanics firm.
